title: Rudolf Blaschka 1892 transport / handoff working ledger
purpose: Recast the 1892 journey and Ware commission from a person-first itinerary into independently moving entities, handoff episodes, regulatory encounters, media conversions and asynchronous reassembly. This file is a research ledger, not a public-map data source yet.
methodological_guards: A handoff is recorded only when a source supports movement, receipt, transfer, inspection, unpacking, preservation, forwarding, delayed arrival or conversion of medium.
Passenger customs, bonded freight and museum customs inspection remain separate events even when they involve the same institutional label.
Sampled good condition is not generalized to an unopened whole shipment.
Final damage is not assigned to a transport stage unless the source identifies the stage or actor.
The June 1892 repair of two severely damaged models is not assigned to U.B. 346–350; Goodale says they came in the first consignment.
Later packing procedures are comparative evidence only and are not back-projected as the exact 1892 crate architecture.
Taxon-level continuity does not prove a unique one-to-one genealogy from a specific field reference to a specific finished model.

working_claim: The 1892 expedition and Ware commission form a coupled counterflow system in which maker, finished glass, botanical references, seeds, instructions, preserved specimens, books and later models travel through different infrastructures and clocks. The workshop operates at distance by decomposing work into transportable media and by reassembling them through handoffs that redistribute authority over opening, classification, preservation, repair, selection and display.
